title: Reliability Covenant — 12-week cross-team sprint playground and run-to-stable plan
content:
Purpose

This doc captures a practical, lightweight cross-team plan for a 12-week reliability sprint we’re calling the "Reliability Covenant". The goal: converge on pragmatic SLOs, test orchestration patterns (routing/fallback), and prove an operational handoff that reduces incident toil by 30% for model-serving flows.

Why a "covenant"?
- Emphasizes shared commitments across product, serving-runtime, SRE, and platform teams.
- Keeps it social and contractual (small, signed agreements per service).

Scope
- Primary surface: model-serving (text generation + embeddings) endpoints and routing layer.
- Included teams: platform-engineering (owner), serving-runtime, site-reliability, product-hosted-api, devexp for SDK hooks.
- Out of scope (for this 12-week run): private deploy installs beyond internal QA, experimental model weights onboarding.

Success criteria (end of 12 weeks) — measurable outcomes
- SLOs defined and agreed for 3 representative services (baseline: p50/p95 latency, availability window, error-rate).
- Automated SLO dashboard (per-route) with live alerts ≠ pager noise (<= 2 false alarms/week).
- Two safety-net playbooks implemented: regional fallback + model-variant fallback with smoke tests.
- Incident toil reduced (hand tracking) by >= 30% on those services (compare 30-day before/after).

Top-level milestones (12-week cadence)
- Week 0–2: Discovery + Service selection + baseline metrics collection
  - Identify 3 candidate services (low, med, high QPS)
  - Pull historic traces: latency distributions, error classes, traffic shape (seq len)
  - Draft SLO proposals per service (owner: product + SRE)

- Week 3–5: Agreement & instrumentation
  - Finalize SLO thresholds + error budget policy (burn-rate windows)
  - Implement/enable metric collection (latency buckets, request-level tags) and add to dashboard template
  - Add simple synthetic canaries for model-variant fallback

- Week 6–8: Orchestration experiments & canary rollouts
  - Run traffic-split experiments (10/90 -> 50/50) for fallback patterns
  - Test automatic fallback triggers (e.g., sustained p95 > threshold for 2m)
  - Evaluate cost vs latency trade-offs for quantized model variant fallback

- Week 9–12: Stabilize + runbook + handoff
  - Freeze SLOs & publish operational covenant docs
  - Run cross-team tabletop + simulated outage walk-throughs
  - Handoff steady-state ownership and QBR metric checkpoints

Roles & responsibilities (lightweight)
- Platform-engineering (lead): coordinate timelines, host dashboards, manage infra changes for routing experiments.
- Serving-runtime: provide model-variant compatibility guarantees, KV cache implications, and runtime flags for fallbacks.
- Site-reliability: define SLI collection, alert thresholds, and ownership for pagers.
- Product-hosted-api: approve user-impacted SLO targets and customer communication plan.
- Developer-experience: ensure SDKs expose route-level observability hooks and client-side retry guidance.

Communication plan
- Weekly 30m sync on Thursdays: quick blockers, metric snapshots, decision log updates (owner: Priya)
- #reliability-updates Slack channel for async status; tag "slo-covenant" threads
- Confluence canonical page (INFRA-SLO-GUIDE-324) for final artifacts and signed covenants

Decision log template (short)
- Date | Decision | Rationale | Impacted services | Approver(s) | Jira link
- Example: 2026-02-19 | Use p95 latency 350ms for text-gen-prod | historical 90th at 320ms + 10% buffer | text-gen-prod | Priya, Ethan | PLAT-9182

Quick implementation checklist (initial run)
- [ ] Pick 3 services + owners
- [ ] Pull 30/90-day telemetry and attach to proposal
- [ ] Define SLOs and error budget policy doc per service
- [ ] Build dashboard template (p50/p95/p99, errors, burn-rate)
- [ ] Wire alerts -> oncall rotation (SRE) with tuning windows
- [ ] Implement fallback policy prototype (routing + model variant)
- [ ] Run two controlled traffic experiments and collect results
- [ ] Run tabletop incident + upload after-action notes

Operational notes & heuristics (less formal, notes-to-self style)
- Keep alerts tiered: page for sustained customer impact (>= 5m error rate spike), slack for short-lived blips.
- Combine telemetry sources: LB logs + runtime token-metrics + synthetic probes. Don’t rely on a single source for SLA firing.
- Prefix caching can mask cold-starts — ensure synthetic probe hits cold path every 6h.
- For model-variant fallback, measure quality delta (small set of golden prompts) in parallel; do not blindly fall back on lower-quality variant without quality gating.

Open questions (for review meeting)
- How strict should product be about quality regressions during fallback? threshold? (suggest: max 5% decrease on eval set)
- Where does cost allocation land if fallbacks increase token units? (finance input needed)
- Should canaries be user-facing or internal only? (risk tolerance discussion)

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: noisy alerts -> pager fatigue. Mitigation: aggressive suppression during experiments + temporary slack-only notifications until thresholds dialed.
- Risk: fallback reduces quality and causes user complaints. Mitigation: quality shadowing and rollback automation + comms plan.
- Risk: instrumentation gaps. Mitigation: freeze on a small set of telemetry items and require sign-off before experiment.

Appendix: useful links and artifacts (working list)
- Confluence: INFRA-SLO-GUIDE-324 (draft SLO patterns)
- Jira: PLAT-9182 (orchestration experiment epic), SRE-2023 (alert tuning tasks)
- GitHub: repo/platform/slo-orchestration#45 (prototype routing code), repo/monitoring/dashboards#12 (dashboard template)
- Slack: #reliability-updates, #serving-runtime-experiments

Next steps (this week)
- Priya: finalize service candidates and circulate baseline telemetry snapshot (by Fri)
- Ethan + Mei: prototype dashboard template and a synthetic probe script (POC)
- Rafael: draft fallback policy text (3 short bullets) and send to product for feedback

Notes (informal)
- Keep things small and reversible. The point of the covenant is mutual confidence, not heavy governance.
- If we can reduce incident context-switch time by 15% in first month we should celebrate.
